name: Polymarket Analysis Bot
description: Analyzes Polymarket events for coordinated bot activity, suspicious holder concentration, and off-platform social amplification. Ingests every analysis as a DKG Knowledge Assertion in the user's chosen Context Graph so findings are queryable, shareable, and promotable to Verified Memory.

security.notes: The MCP server itself talks to two endpoints only: the local DKG node (default 127.0.0.1:9200) and Umanitek's hosted analysis service (Polymarket Analysis API on EC2). All third-party API keys (Polymarket, LunarCrush) live on the EC2 service — the user never provides them and the MCP server never sees them. Writes to DKG are limited to creating named assertions in the user's chosen Context Graph (POST /api/assertion/create) and writing analysis quads into those assertions (POST /api/assertion/{name}/write); no PUBLISH (VM) or SHARE (SWM promotion) operations are performed by the integration itself. The npm package has no postinstall, install, or preinstall scripts. The hosted EC2 service enforces per-IP rate limiting and a body-size cap so abusive scripted use is bounded; see the project's api_service.py for the active limits.

promotionPath: Each analyze_market call creates a named Assertion in the caller's selected Context Graph (Working Memory) containing the full risk report — market metadata, risk score, top market movers, suspicious comment clusters, and LunarCrush social-amplification overlap — as RDF quads under the http://dkg.io/ontology/polymarket/ vocabulary. The agent or operator can then SPARQL-query the assertion, cross-reference it against other on-graph evidence, and explicitly promote it to Shared Memory for team review. From SWM, a subsequent PUBLISH operation anchors the analysis on-chain as a Verified Memory Knowledge Asset whose UAL becomes oracle-consumable evidence for downstream agents working on the same paranet's election-integrity, market-manipulation, or compliance use cases.
fitNotes: Plugs directly into the LLM-Wiki / autoresearch direction: prediction-market manipulation is a domain where attribution and verifiability matter as much as the analysis itself, and DKG's WM→SWM→VM promotion chain provides exactly that audit trail. A coding agent or research agent operating on a Context Graph can call analyze_market on any Polymarket event URL and immediately have a structured, queryable, attributable evidence node it can reason over — without re-running the heavy analysis pipeline (held off-graph in the EC2 service) and without ever touching upstream API keys.
